name: clean-code-no-links
known_outcome: Two open issues and no dependency between them: #387 names #385 only as provenance. The sweep wrote nothing.

issues.title: Ship the clean-code standards as Laravel Boost guidelines, and remove every comment from code and the ruleset
issues.body:
## Problem

**Agents cannot see the standards until the linter rejects their code.**

- The standards live on mikebronner.dev/clean-code, in `docs/standards/` (73 documents) and in `docs/phpmd/` (35).
- Laravel Boost loads none of these.
- An agent in a consuming project therefore writes code, fails `phpcs`, and fixes it afterwards.
- It should write compliant code from the start.

**Comments drift, and the ruleset is mostly comments.**

Measured on `main` at `4c05dc6`:

| Location | Comment lines |
|---|---|
| `CleanCode/ruleset.xml` | 3,297 of 3,557 (93%), for 57 `<rule ref>` entries |
| `CleanCode/**/*.php` | 1,746 |
| `tests/` (excluding fixtures) | ~22,900 |

- #384 closed as completed, but its `rules.xml` criterion was never met.
- `4c05dc6` removed three test docblocks that still claimed a PHP 8.1 floor and an 8.4-only CI.

**How the two halves connect:** once the guidelines and `docs/standards/` hold the reasoning, a code comment has nothing left to say.

## Part 1: Boost guidelines

Ship one guideline per documented standard under `resources/boost/guidelines/`. The goal is that an agent follows the standards while it writes code.

Each guideline:
- States the rule, with a short example of compliant code and of non-compliant code.
- Names every sniff code that enforces the rule, for example `CleanCode.Conditionals.DisallowElse`.
- Says whether each sniff is auto-fixable by `phpcbf`.
- For a standard no sniff can check, says it is enforced by code review only. That covers Tier 3 standards such as `classes-contracts-interfaces`.
- Links the matching `docs/standards/*.md`.

The source of truth is the mikebronner.dev content. Wherever a guideline and `docs/standards/` disagree, fix the disagreement. Do not copy it.

**Boost discovery limits.** These were verified against Boost v2.9.1, and the README must state them:
- Boost loads a package's guidelines only when the consumer's `boost.json` lists the package under `packages`.
- The package must be a direct Composer dependency. A package pulled in transitively gets nothing.
- Boost versions before v2.9.1 keep only the last guideline file from each package.

Whether each guideline applies to agent-only development is tracked in mikebronner/mikebronner.me#22. That discussion stays out of these guidelines.

## Part 2: Remove comments

- **PHP:** remove every comment from all PHP under `CleanCode/` and `tests/`.
  - Keep functional directives (`phpcs:ignore`, `phpcs:disable`, `phpcs:enable`).
  - `tests/fixtures/` is excluded, because fixtures are sniff input.
- **Rulesets:** in `CleanCode/ruleset.xml`, `phpcs.self.xml` and `phpunit.xml.dist`, keep only one-line comments that label a group of rules, for example `<!-- Conditionals -->`.
- Removed comments are deleted, not moved into docs. Git history and the linked issues keep their reasoning.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every standard in `docs/standards/` has a guideline under `resources/boost/guidelines/`. Each guideline names its enforcing sniff codes or states that it is enforced by code review only.
- [ ] A throwaway Laravel project that requires this package directly, and whose `boost.json` lists the package, receives every guideline after `boost:install`.
- [ ] The README documents the `boost.json` requirement, the direct-dependency requirement and the Boost version floor.
- [ ] No comment remains in PHP under `CleanCode/` or `tests/` (fixtures excluded), except `phpcs:*` directives.
- [ ] The three XML files contain only one-line group labels.
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` states the no-comment rule.
- [ ] `composer test` and `composer lint` stay green.
- [ ] The error count from `composer lint:self` does not increase. Measure before and after, because #384 found that removing annotations changes which codes some sniffs report.

issues.title: Ship Boost guidelines for the PHPMD-port sniffs documented only in docs/phpmd/
issues.body:
📋 Follow-up from Holmes's review of #385 (PR #386).

🔍 **Observation:** 16 loaded `CleanCode.*` sniffs are named in no Boost guideline. Each is a PHPMD port documented only in `docs/phpmd/`.

📍 **Location:** `CleanCode/Sniffs/` (auto-registered by the `CleanCode` standard) and `docs/phpmd/*.md`.

💡 **Why it's worth doing:** #385 exists so that agents write compliant code before `phpcs` runs. Its guidelines cover `docs/standards/` only. An agent in a consuming project still meets these 16 rules only when the linter rejects its code.

🏷️ **Tracked under:** systemic-debt

## ✅ Sniffs with no guideline

- [ ] `CleanCode.Naming.LongVariable`
- [ ] `CleanCode.Naming.LongClassName`
- [ ] `CleanCode.Naming.BooleanGetMethodName`
- [ ] `CleanCode.Metrics.CyclomaticComplexity`
- [ ] `CleanCode.Metrics.NPathComplexity`
- [ ] `CleanCode.Metrics.DepthOfInheritance`
- [ ] `CleanCode.Metrics.NumberOfChildren`
- [ ] `CleanCode.Functions.ExcessiveMethodLength`
- [ ] `CleanCode.Functions.ExcessiveParameterList`
- [ ] `CleanCode.Functions.DisallowBooleanArgumentFlag`
- [ ] `CleanCode.Arrays.DuplicatedArrayKey`
- [ ] `CleanCode.Conditionals.DisallowListAssignmentInCondition`
- [ ] `CleanCode.ControlStructures.DisallowCountInLoopExpression`
- [ ] `CleanCode.ControlStructures.DisallowExitExpression`
- [ ] `CleanCode.Controversial.Superglobals`
- [ ] `CleanCode.Debug.DisallowDebugFunctions`

⏭️ `CleanCode.Naming.ShortVariable` and `CleanCode.Naming.ShortClassName` are left off on purpose. They enforce a rule the semantic-naming guideline already states. PR #386 fixes them.

## 🔀 Open decision for triage

There are two ways to close this. One is a guideline per `docs/phpmd/` page. The other folds each sniff into the existing guideline whose rule it enforces. The second keeps the one-guideline-per-standard shape #385 chose.

## 🟡 Non-blocking

This sits outside #385's acceptance criteria. It is also outside the unit PR #386 delivers. #385 scopes its guidelines to `docs/standards/`.
